conventions.convention: The metric has signature (−,+,+,+); u is a smooth future-directed unit timelike congruence with g(u,u)=−1. SI length coordinates use x⁰=ct and dimensionless observer components.
The state domain X is nonempty and open in (0,∞)×R; e is C², and the spacetime state map is C². Define n=1/v, s=nσp, ε=ne, T=e_σp, p=−e_v, H=e+pv, and μ=H−Tσp.

The selected fixed-composition material adopts T>0, energy including rest energy, and continuum parcel energy E=N e(V/N,S/N), with real N>0 and V>0. This is a local constitutive assumption, without global gravitating additivity.
The perfect branch adopts J=nu, stress εu⊗u+p(g⁻¹+u⊗u), and zero covariant divergences of both currents; no external force, dissipative flux, or arbitrary-data existence assertion is included.

Circulation uses P=(H/c)u♭ and the u-flow parameter λ. Conservation requires constant specific entropy on the swept region; advection Dσp=0 alone is insufficient. The geometric supplier chain carries Countable Choice.

load_bearing.statement: On the stated smooth fixed-composition branch with C² state data and T>0, adopt Jᵃ=nuᵃ and stress εuᵃuᵇ+p(gᵃᵇ+uᵃuᵇ), with ∇ₐJᵃ=0 and ∇ₐTᵃᵇ=0. These are physical model assumptions, without an arbitrary-data solution-existence claim.
In the adopted C² fixed-composition local-equilibrium model, dε=T ds+μ dn, ε+p=Ts+μn, and dp=s dT+n dμ. On the positive open parcel domain, E=N e(V/N,S/N) satisfies dE=T dS−p dV+μ dN and E=TS−pV+μN.

Under the isolated perfect-material assumptions with n,T>0 and the stated compact closed curve and local-flow hypotheses, ∇ₐ(suᵃ)=0, Dσp=0, and C′(λ)=c⁻¹∫γλ T dσp. Circulation is locally constant if σp is constant on the whole swept region.

concerns.concern: The Borghini locator says “PDF pp. 4–5 and 134–148” for local equilibrium and relativistic entropy balance. In the available 184-page 2015 PDF, PDF pp. 4–5 are contents pages; local equilibrium is on PDF pp. 13–15, and §IX.3.2 entropy conservation is on PDF p. 149 (printed p. 141). The section references support the formulation, but the PDF locators need correction.

The Borghini locator says “PDF pp. 4–5 and 148” for local equilibrium and the thermodynamic identity used in the entropy calculation. In the available 184-page 2015 PDF, PDF pp. 4–5 are contents pages, local equilibrium is on PDF pp. 13–15, and §IX.3.2 with the thermodynamic identities and entropy proof is on PDF p. 149. PDF p. 148 instead continues the perfect-stress decomposition.

The Borghini locator assigns conditional entropy-current conservation to “PDF pp. 134–148”, but the cited §IX.3.2 and equation (IX.22) occur on PDF p. 149 (printed p. 141) of the available 184-page 2015 PDF. The mathematical deduction is supported independently; this is a locator error.

alerts.finding: Its Borghini locator says “§§IX.2, IX.3.1, and IX.4.1–IX.4.2 (PDF pp. 137–147)” for currents, decompositions, and frame choices. seams_checked.note: The material postulate and first-law theorem preserve the supplied C² state function, positive temperature, rest-energy convention, real continuum marker amount, parcel domain, and SI normalization. Neither converts these premises into empirical facts or global gravitating extensivity.

The entropy theorem uses the isolated f=0 specialization with n,T>0 and the exact compact-loop/local-flow circulation interface. It retains draft supplier status and AC_ω, and separately supplies the zero-derivative-to-constancy argument. It does not infer circulation conservation from entropy advection alone.

The downstream postulate retains the perfect-state and stress conventions, adds a prescribed uniform Minkowski reference state and h₀>0, and explicitly adopts its effective linear systems. Its linear response conclusions do not claim nonlinear existence or error estimates from the perfect-fluid postulate.
